messages:
maria: Quick report: after the recent `exports` map change, our Vite SSR sample deployed to Vercel Edge errors with `TypeError: RedwoodClient is not a constructor`. Works in Node SSR but fails on Edge.

oliver: Hmm. Which entry did the bundler pick? The package now has `import` and `require` conditionals, right?

maria: Yes. Package.json exports has `import: ./dist/index.mjs` and `require: ./dist/index.cjs`. Vite's SSR build ends up bundling the CJS file into the edge bundle.

kevin: That can flip the exports shape. If the CJS build doesn't preserve named exports, consumers doing `import { RedwoodClient } from` will break at runtime.

zoe: Any runtime stacktrace?

maria: Short: `at Object.<anonymous> (edge-handler.js:10:34) TypeError: RedwoodClient is not a constructor`. Inspecting bundle shows `var r = require('./index.cjs'); const RedwoodClient = r.RedwoodClient || r.default;` but `r.default` is an init function.

oliver: Two fixes: (1) republish CJS with proper named exports (build tool flag), or (2) add explicit subpath exports like `./edge`: `./dist/index.mjs` so bundlers don't fall back to CJS for edge targets.

kevin: Also add a short note in DevEx docs: for SSR on edge, set resolver mainFields to ['module','browser','main'] or alias the import to the .mjs entry as a temporary workaround.

zoe: I'll open RED-DEVEX-4201 to track: remove legacy CJS shim, add edge subpath, and add CI check that imports both with `require()` and dynamic `import()` to validate shapes.

ci-bot: new issue created: RED-DEVEX-4201 - "exports map: fix edge SSR interop" (assigned to zoe)

maria: Thanks. I'll add a tiny repro and link it in the issue.
